URL: https://understandingwar.org/research/middle-east/iran-update-special-report-may-19-2026/
TITLE: Iran Update Special Report, May 19, 2026
PUBLISHED: 2026-05-19 21:49 UTC
AUTHOR: Nadia Sleiman (ISW/CTP)

KEY TAKEAWAYS:
1. US continues to pressure Iran economically through naval blockade and sanctions; especially affecting oil exports
2. Concerns from Iranian officials/citizens about economic damage do NOT alone imply Iranian leaders will drop negotiating demands
3. Some NATO countries support plan to escort ships through Strait of Hormuz starting EARLY JULY if Iran continues blockade (Bloomberg May 19)
4. Iran reportedly analysed US military aircraft flight patterns to improve targeting

CENTCOM:
- 88 commercial vessels redirected (up from 85 yesterday)
- 4 disabled since April 13 blockade began

IRAN OIL STORAGE CRISIS:
- Iran expanded oil storage by reusing 10 AGING TANKERS to hold oil (per UANI + FT)
- Clustered around Kharg Island and Chabahar Port
- Kpler: Iran stored 42 million barrels on Iranian tankers in Middle East (65% increase since conflict began)
- ~24 million more barrels in floating storage on empty tankers within US blockade area
- Kayrros: onshore storage at 64% capacity; only "a few weeks' worth of oil production space"

US TREASURY (May 19):
- Sanctioned Amin Exchange + associated front companies (hundreds of millions in oil transactions)
- Blocked 19 vessels linked to illicit Iranian oil exports
- Urged global partners to enforce sanctions more strictly

IRANIAN DOMESTIC PRESSURE:
- President Masoud Pezeshkian called for long-term planning to mitigate war-related economic impacts (May 19)
- Officials warned of rising drug prices potentially fueling public discontent
- Anti-regime media: gasoline shortages, worker protest in Zanjan City over wages (May 19)

NATO HORMUZ ESCORT PLAN:
- Senior NATO official to Bloomberg May 19: countries considering Hormuz ship escort beginning early July
- Several NATO countries support; NOT unanimous required support yet
- Some NATO countries still reluctant to get involved
- General concern about economic consequences of keeping strait closed

NYT/RUSSIA-IRAN COOPERATION:
- NYT: Iranian military commanders studied US fighter jets and bombers flight patterns
- US official said US-aware of risk
- Aircraft losses indicating predictability: F-15E + A-10 downed April 3; F-35 damaged March 19
- Russia "may have supported this effort" + provided satellite imagery of US bases + modified Shahed drones

US-IRAN NEGOTIATIONS:
- Reuters (citing 2 Iranian officials May 18): US agreed to release 25% of frozen Iranian assets under unspecified timetable
- Iran sought complete release
- Iran sought enrichment pause shorter than 20-year US demand
- Iran proposed diluting some HEU + sending rest to Russia (right to "reclaim" if US violates)
- US demand: hand over HEU to US, dismantle Iranian nuclear facilities

HEZBOLLAH:
- ~11 attacks per day since April 16 ceasefire start
- IED ambushes resumed May 13 on Qouzah axis (central south Lebanon) + Taybeh-Qantara axis (SE Lebanon)
- Israeli public broadcaster Kan: Hezbollah FPV drones affected 70-80% of Israeli forces' freedom of movement in southern Lebanon (restricting most to nighttime)
- FPV drones now cause majority of IDF deaths since April 16 ceasefire

OTHER AXIS:
- Total 6 drones from Iraq → UAE in past 48 hrs (May 17-19) per UAE Defense Ministry
- Iranian-backed Iraqi militia Kataib Hezbollah warning of retaliation
- Iraqi militias using surveillance drones to observe Saudi Arabia + Kuwait (per Reuters May 13)
- IRGC media accused ISRAEL of UAE drone strike to drive wedge with UAE
